And concerning this year, the astrologers had predicted and said
that rains would be abundant,
and rivers would overflow,
and Baghdad would be entirely flooded and destroyed.
Yet from when the year began until it ended, not a drop of rain fell upon the earth,
and the springs dried up;
and thus the astrologers were put to shame.
At this time was known Abu'l-Hasan Thabit, of the pagan Harranians,
who was the son of Qurrah,
son of Marwan,
son of Qiyura,
son of Abraham,
son of Qiyura,
son of Marinus,
son of Solomon.
This man was formerly a money-changer in the market of Harran,
then he devoted himself to philosophy in a most admirable manner.
And he was thoroughly proficient in three languages:
in Greek, Syriac, and Arabic.
For he composed in Arabic about one hundred and fifty books on logic, mathematics, astronomy, and medicine.
And in Syriac he wrote about sixteen books, most of which we have seen and possessed:
A book on the laws and canons of the pagans.
A book on the burial of the dead.
A book on the confirmation of the religion of the pagans.
A book on purity and impurity.
A book on the animals that are suitable for offering sacrifices from them.
A book on the times of prayers.
A book on the readings that are appropriate for each one of the seven planets in the prayers.
A book on repentance and supplication.
A book on music.
A book of the history of the ancient Syrian kings, who are the Chaldeans.
A book on the religion of the Sabians.
A book on the division of the days of the week among the seven planets.
A book on the nobility of his race and his ancestors, from whom they are descended.
A book of the laws of Hermes and his prayers, those with which the pagans pray.
A book on the proposition:
that two straight lines,
when they are produced at less than two right angles,
meet one another.
Another book on the same subject.
For he said {OCR?} in one of his treatises, when praising Harran and paganism, as follows:
"While many were subjected to error by means of torture,
our own fathers, by God, endured and spoke valiantly,
and this blessed city was never defiled by the error of Nazareth.
